\subsection{Planet or Not?}
\emph{Three tests try to reject a transit candidate, and some candidates cannot be decided: learn what a passed checklist means and what it does not} \quad 8 steps, 6 of them graded, 6-10 min, Introductory astronomy.

undefined

\subsection{Why We Cannot See Earth From Here}
\emph{Two separate problems stand between a telescope and a planet, an angle and a contrast: see why a planet like Earth at ten parsecs is out of reach, and why λ/D is not a coronagraph’s inner working angle} \quad 6 steps, 4 of them graded, 6-10 min, Introductory astronomy.

undefined

\subsection{Architectures}
\emph{The planets we have imaged and the planets of the Solar System on one log diagram: see what direct imaging can find, and why that is not a picture of the planets that exist} \quad 6 steps, 4 of them graded, 6-10 min, Introductory astronomy.

undefined

\subsection{What Is It Made Of?}
\emph{A planet’s density is only as good as its star: see how much of the uncertainty is the star’s, and what a density can and cannot say} \quad 7 steps, 5 of them graded, 6-10 min, Introductory astronomy.

undefined

\subsection{How Many Earths?}
\emph{From the planets a survey found to how many there are: what it could have seen, what a count becomes, and what a bin cannot say} \quad 7 steps, 5 of them graded, 8-12 min, Introductory to upper-level astronomy.

undefined

\subsection{The Metallicity Term}
\emph{Add the metal content of a galaxy to the Cepheid period-luminosity relation, see what it does to a distance and to its error, and see where the cited term stops being tested} \quad 7 steps, 5 of them graded, 8-12 min, Upper-level astronomy.

undefined

\subsection{The Clock That Drifts}
\emph{Measure when a planet transits, plot how far each transit is from a steady clock, and read the slow wave a second planet writes} \quad 8 steps, 5 of them graded, 10-14 min, Introductory astronomy.

undefined

\subsection{Deep or Wide?}
\emph{The same nights can reach faint sources over a small area or bright ones over a large one: which finds more depends on the class of source} \quad 6 steps, 4 of them graded, 8-14 min, Introductory astronomy.

undefined

\subsection{Two Telescopes, One Question}
\emph{The same depth over the same area with a one-meter telescope and an 8.4-meter one: how much longer does the small one take, and why} \quad 5 steps, 3 of them graded, 5-9 min, Introductory astronomy.

undefined

\subsection{Propose an Observation}
\emph{Design a survey for a stated goal, predict what it will find, check it against the model and justify the plan: many plans are right} \quad 4 steps, 2 of them graded, 6-12 min, Upper-level astronomy.

undefined

\subsection{Which Instrument for Which Question?}
\emph{Five facilities from the instrument library, the same faint star, and what decides the choice: light, sampling, field and wavelength} \quad 10 steps, 8 of them graded, 10-15 min, Majors and upper-level astronomy.

\subsection{The Sky Background}
\emph{The sky is a light of its own: how bright it is inside a star’s aperture, what a brighter sky costs in exposure, and when the Moon matters} \quad 12 steps, 10 of them graded, 12-18 min, Majors and upper-level astronomy.

\subsection{From Photons to a Number}
\emph{The whole chain as one traced calculation: electrons, noise, signal-to-noise, magnitude, calibration, and the uncertainty carried at each step} \quad 10 steps, 8 of them graded, 12-18 min, Majors and upper-level astronomy.
